cards.title: Communicate real availability before the purchase decision
cards.summary: Give customers accurate stock and timing information while their options remain open.
cards.use_when: Sequencing an offer: when in the funnel to introduce urgency vs. lock in the commitment.

cards.title: Why scarcity works: availability as a quality shortcut
cards.summary: Scarcity works partly because availability is usually a valid shortcut for quality, and partly because lost freedom triggers reactance — understand both to use it responsibly.
cards.use_when: Evaluating whether low-stock or exclusivity messaging is truthful and appropriate for a product page.

cards.title: Restricted access increases perceived value of content and products
cards.summary: When access to information or material is officially restricted, people want it more and rate it as better — even without consuming it.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to gate content, run a members-only drop, or restrict a product to a customer segment.

cards.title: Scarcity changes desire, not utility value
cards.summary: Scarce items gain desirability but not real quality, so scarcity-based pricing is justified only for possession value, not performance.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much of a premium to put on limited-edition or scarce stock, and how to describe it on the PDP.

cards.title: Inconsistently available stock makes customers rebellious
cards.summary: Applying rules or privileges erratically sets an expectation that can't be withdrawn without a backlash, so maintain consistent stock and policy availability.
cards.use_when: Managing recurring inventory, restock policies, subscription availability, or inconsistent promo practices.

cards.title: Use genuine inventory scarcity without implying better product quality
cards.summary: Limited availability can increase desire to own a product without improving its functional value.
cards.use_when: Planning or reviewing an ecommerce offer, product page or campaign.

cards.title: Separate competitive urgency from product fit in limited drops
cards.summary: Competition for a scarce item can rush decisions; a drop still needs a clear value proposition.
cards.use_when: Planning or reviewing an ecommerce offer, product page or campaign.

cards.title: Use verified shortcuts to simplify ecommerce purchase decisions
cards.summary: Shoppers under information load may rely on a few salient cues; those cues should accurately summarize relevant evidence.
cards.use_when: Planning or reviewing an ecommerce offer, product page or campaign.

cards.title: Audit social-proof creative for fabricated evidence
cards.summary: Social proof becomes misleading when actors or staged reactions are presented as genuine customer experiences.
cards.use_when: Planning or reviewing an ecommerce offer, product page or campaign.

cards.title: Diagnose Growth Bottlenecks Through a Data-Integrity First Lens
cards.summary: Treat business growth as a sequence of bottlenecks and use trustworthy data to find the current one before spending more on creative or account structure.
cards.use_when: You feel like the store is 'on a treadmill' — dashboards show improving ROAS but profit and revenue are flat, and you need to decide where to focus resources (merchandise, creative, media, retention) next quarter.

cards.title: Stop Northstar-ing on Platform-Reported ROAS
cards.summary: Platform ROAS is not comparable across campaigns, platforms or funnel stages because each read reflects different margins, attribution models and funnel positions.
cards.use_when: You are setting KPI targets, evaluating channel performance, or deciding how to reallocate budget across Meta, Google, Pinterest or TikTok.

cards.title: Cut the Three Sources of ROAS Over-Inflation
cards.summary: View-through attribution, existing-customer bleed-over and third-party halo effects all inflate platform ROAS above true incremental impact.
cards.use_when: You suspect your reported ROAS is too good to be true, or you are auditing why higher ad spend is not translating to higher profit.

cards.title: Set Meta Attribution Windows to 7-Day Click / 1-Day Engaged
cards.summary: Removing 1-day view-through from Meta reporting produces a ROAS read that correlates more tightly with P&L efficiency.
cards.use_when: You are configuring Meta campaign reporting or diagnosing why Meta ROAS does not reconcile with actual profit.

cards.title: Use Meta Incremental Attribution as Directional, Not Definitive
cards.summary: Meta's incremental attribution is an industry-benchmark estimate built from competitors' lift tests, not a live holdout measurement in your account.
cards.use_when: You want a more causal channel read but cannot afford a full geo-lift or platform lift test, and are deciding whether to trust the incremental attribution column.

cards.title: Build a Metric Hierarchy Instead of Adding More Dashboards
cards.summary: Subtract metrics rather than add them — the goal is the fewest commercially-aligned KPIs that allow clear decisions.
cards.use_when: Your team has multiple attribution tools and dashboards producing conflicting reads, and meetings stall because no one agrees which number is right.

cards.title: Distinguish MER from AMER to Avoid False Scaling Decisions
cards.summary: Total MER can rise on returning-customer revenue while new-customer acquisition quietly deteriorates; AMER isolates the acquisition spend's true efficiency.
cards.use_when: You review monthly marketing efficiency and are deciding whether to increase (or cut) media budget.

cards.title: Track New-Customer Revenue, Orders, CAC and Profit Contribution
cards.summary: A compact set of finance-grade metrics shows whether acquisition is growing, efficient and profitable — the core of an executive dashboard.
cards.use_when: You are designing your weekly or monthly store performance dashboard and want metrics that tie directly to profit rather than platform attribution.

cards.title: Use LTGP:CAC as a Comparable Cross-Business Metric
cards.summary: A ratio linking lifetime gross profit to acquisition cost is comparable across time and across businesses, unlike MER or AMER.
cards.use_when: You want to self-benchmark historically, compare portfolio or competitor efficiency, or decide how aggressively to scale acquisition.

cards.title: Tag COGS in Shopify to See Real-Time Gross Margin Compression
cards.summary: Without tagged cost of goods you cannot see margin compression during discount events, so profit, LTGP and contribution metrics will be wrong.
cards.use_when: You are preparing for Black Friday or any discount event and relying on a fixed gross-margin assumption in your reporting or agency models.

cards.title: Run a Geo-Lift Experiment to Measure True Incremental ROAS
cards.summary: A controlled state/region test with a counterfactual prediction reveals the causal revenue impact of a spend change when attribution is confounded.
cards.use_when: You are a larger brand deciding how much budget to put into a channel, or whether a top-of-funnel investment (TikTok, OOH, YouTube) actually drives revenue.

cards.title: Understand Platform Lift Tests vs External Geo-Lift Tests
cards.summary: In-platform lift tests split at the user level; external geo-lift splits at the region level — each has different trust and cost trade-offs.
cards.use_when: You want to validate a channel's incremental impact but need to choose between running a Meta/TikTok/Google lift test or building your own geo-lift.

cards.title: Don't Chase First-Click or Third-Party Attribution Truth
cards.summary: The most valuable journey points are first and last click, but first click is effectively unknowable and third-party tools add confusion rather than truth.
cards.use_when: You are evaluating third-party attribution tools or deciding how to allocate budget between brand search, top-of-funnel and bottom-of-funnel campaigns.

cards.title: Reconcile Platform Data Against the P&L
cards.summary: The core discipline of data integrity is tying platform metrics back to actual financial outcomes so decisions rest on the P&L, not on attribution reads.
cards.use_when: You are auditing your measurement setup or preparing a board/CFO review of marketing spend efficiency.

cards.title: Audit for the Common Tracking Infrastructure Failures
cards.summary: Recurring measurement mistakes — view-through defaults, untagged COGS, customer-list leakage, missing CAPI — recur across audits and should be checked systematically.
cards.use_when: You are running an internal audit or ad-account health check and want a repeatable list of things to verify.

cards.title: Platform lift tests vs geo-lift tests: choosing your incrementality method
cards.summary: Compare in-platform lift experiments and geo-lift experiments on speed, cost, verifiability, and effort so you pick the right one for your paid media validation.
cards.use_when: You need to validate whether a paid channel (Meta, TikTok, Google, YouTube) is driving genuinely incremental purchases rather than just claiming credit for existing demand.

cards.title: Using causal impact / counterfactual modeling for retroactive channel analysis
cards.summary: Apply Google's open-source causal impact package to retrospectively estimate what revenue would have been without a channel intervention, using third-party confounding variables.
cards.use_when: You introduced a channel or campaign (e.g., YouTube, TikTok) at some point in the past and want a directional retrospective read on whether it actually drove revenue.

cards.title: Why launch timing confuses channel results (Black Friday and Q4 era)
cards.summary: Brands wrongly credit a new channel for a strong period because they launched it during seasonality peaks without any measurement system.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to keep a channel you launched in October/November or during any peak season based on a good subsequent month.

cards.title: Setting up Conversions API (CAPI) on Meta for better tracking and optimization
cards.summary: Route purchase events server-side through Meta's Conversions API to bypass unreliable browser tracking and improve event matching and optimization.
cards.use_when: You are auditing or fixing Meta ad tracking for an ecommerce store and want to improve data quality feeding the ad platform.

cards.title: Avoid Shopify marketing/attribution reports for decisions
cards.summary: The source finds Shopify's marketing and attribution reports unreliable and recommends not using them for business decisions.
cards.use_when: You are setting up your measurement stack for an ecommerce store and deciding which data sources to trust for spend and revenue decisions.

cards.title: Treat GA4 as a redundancy layer, not a daily decision dashboard
cards.summary: GA4 should collect data properly as a fallback, but should not drive day-to-day ecommerce decisions because it offers nothing you can't get from Shopify or the ad platforms.
cards.use_when: You are deciding what to actually open each day to make budget and campaign decisions for your store.

cards.title: One-day view attribution overattribution mistake
cards.summary: Running one-day view through all campaigns inflates reported ROAS with massive overattribution, so remove it to see reality.
cards.use_when: You are auditing Meta (or similar) campaign reporting and wondering why reported ROAS looks great but the business results disagree.

cards.title: Account for Google's halo effect when judging ROAS
cards.summary: Google overattributes by taking credit for conversions that other platforms drove, so its ROAS should be reconsidered with skepticism.
cards.use_when: You are evaluating a PMax or Google campaign showing very high ROAS and deciding whether to increase spend.

cards.title: Brand spend waste caused by over-prioritizing ROAS
cards.summary: Chasing ROAS as the north star leads accounts to leave brand search in, causing large waste even at 8-figure retailers.
cards.use_when: You are structuring paid search or campaign budgets and deciding whether to suppress brand terms.

cards.title: Over-segmentation causes measurement fragmentation
cards.summary: Too many campaigns relative to business complexity and spend fragments data and makes decision-making convoluted.
cards.use_when: You are reviewing account structure and considering splitting campaigns further, or auditing why reporting is hard to interpret.

cards.title: Beware overattribution on low-spend tertiary channels
cards.summary: Small third-party channels like Snapchat, Pinterest, and Reddit show inflated ROAS because low spend defaults to reaching warm pixel audiences rather than driving new growth.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether a small tertiary channel's high ROAS justifies keeping or growing it.

cards.title: Stop existing-customer overspend that inflates metrics
cards.summary: Spending more on existing customers because ROAS looks good inflates all numbers and drives further misallocation.
cards.use_when: You are setting campaign objectives and budgets and need to decide whether to exclude existing customers.

cards.title: Top-funnel Meta objectives (traffic/reach) need a measurement system
cards.summary: Running traffic or reach campaigns on Meta without any measurement system means unmeasurable spend and false confidence drawn from correlation.
cards.use_when: You are considering traffic or reach campaigns for your store, or auditing whether existing ones are justified.

cards.title: DPA overspend driven by attractive ROAS
cards.summary: Scaling dynamic product ads because ROAS looks good leads to non-incremental spend since DPAs sit at the bottom of funnel.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to increase DPA budget based on strong reported ROAS.

cards.title: Build a measurement and testing structure so every decision is validated
cards.summary: Without a testing/experimental design, you cannot validate whether anything is working, which the source considers a core scaling failure.
cards.use_when: You are setting up or auditing the measurement foundation for a store's paid media and need to decide what to test and how.

cards.title: Action items for $1-5M revenue stores: fix reporting basics
cards.summary: At $1-5M revenue, switch to 7-day click on Meta, tag COGS in Shopify, build a profit-focused dashboard, and exclude existing customers from top-of-funnel.
cards.use_when: You run an ecommerce store in the $1-5M revenue range and want the right baseline measurement actions.

cards.title: Action items for $5-20M revenue stores: layer in lift studies
cards.summary: At $5-20M revenue, add in-platform lift studies for top-funnel experimentation and use incremental attribution as a second validation layer beyond 7-day click.
cards.use_when: You run an ecommerce store in the $5-20M revenue range and have the basics in place, ready to add validation infrastructure.

cards.title: Action items for $20M+ revenue stores: geo-lift tests and incrementality factors
cards.summary: At $20M+, run geo-lift tests outside the platform and apply resulting incrementality factors to attributed ROAS numbers for a realistic view.
cards.use_when: You run an ecommerce store at $20M+ revenue with a complex channel and revenue capture mix and need verifiable incrementality measurement.

cards.title: Shift from ROAS to financial-based KPIs for scaling decisions
cards.summary: The source argues winning brands move toward financial-based KPIs and incrementality testing rather than optimizing to platform ROAS.
cards.use_when: You are setting the north-star metric for your store's paid media and deciding what to optimize.

cards.title: Calculate CAC and LTGP monthly as your two core operating metrics
cards.summary: Every DTC brand should compute cost to acquire a customer and constrained lifetime gross profit each month, then treat them as the fundamental diagnostic instead of ROAS.
cards.use_when: You need a single monthly scorecard to decide whether the store can profitably scale paid acquisition, cut spend, or fix retention.

cards.title: Read the LTGP:CAC bands and know what each one demands
cards.summary: LTGP:CAC below 1 is a death spiral, 1-2 needs extremely lean opex, 2-3 is the source's target scaling zone, and above 3 suggests underinvesting in acquisition.
cards.use_when: You are setting a paid-media budget or deciding whether to push spend harder, hold, or pull back on acquisition.

cards.title: Derive CAC from CPM, CTR and conversion rate to offset rising ad costs
cards.summary: CAC = CPC / conversion rate, and CPC = CTR x CPM, so annually rising CPMs can be offset by lifting click-through rate or conversion rate.
cards.use_when: Your CAC is climbing and you need to decide which lever — ad creative, PDP/landing page conversion, or media efficiency — to work on.

cards.title: Split the P&L into first-time and returning customer views
cards.summary: Filter every P&L line by order-type tag to expose an acquisition loss that a combined, blended P&L hides behind returning-customer profit.
cards.use_when: Total profit still looks acceptable but you suspect new-customer acquisition has quietly turned loss-making, or before raising capital or debt.

cards.title: Diagnose the death spiral from the two numbers, not from traffic, creative or seasonality
cards.summary: The spiralling CAC pattern — CAC rises, new customers fall, spend is increased to hold revenue, CAC rises again — is structural and should be diagnosed from the CAC and LTGP series first.
cards.use_when: Revenue or profitability has deteriorated for a quarter and leadership is blaming traffic, creative fatigue, seasonality or the macroeconomy.

cards.title: Rank your measurement methods by distance from base reality
cards.summary: Move up a hierarchy from expert opinion and platform ROAS to multi-regression, quasi-experiments and geo holdouts, because decisions are only as good as how closely the metric tracks reality.
cards.use_when: You need to decide how much to trust a platform-reported number before reallocating budget between channels or scaling spend.

cards.title: Match your CAC discipline to the retention structure of your category
cards.summary: Furniture and homewares should run on first-purchase gross profit with a deliberately flat CAC, while fashion and CPG can extend the LTGP window because repeat revenue genuinely accrues.
cards.use_when: You are setting the measurement window and CAC target for your category, or deciding whether to invest in retention or defend acquisition cost.

cards.title: Use cohort analysis to read retention instead of surface retention metrics
cards.summary: Shopify-style cohort boxes, read forward in time, are the source's required method for measuring lifetime gross profit and retention rather than Klaviyo attributed revenue or daily returning-customer revenue.
cards.use_when: You want to measure retention properly to set your LTGP window and confirm whether recent acquisition cohorts are degrading.

cards.title: Three legitimate ways to fund a sub-1 LTGP:CAC — and who should not use them
cards.summary: Losses on first purchase can be funded by returning-customer profit, investor capital, or debt, but the source warns that capital- and debt-funded models demand an advanced operator.
cards.use_when: You are deliberately losing money on first purchase and must choose how the gap gets financed, or you are evaluating whether to take investment or debt to scale acquisition.

cards.title: Treat operating-expense creep as a separate cash-risk failure mode from the death spiral
cards.summary: Smaller brands can fail from over-invested operating expenses that compress margin, force debt for inventory, and end in a cash constraint rather than a ratio problem.
cards.use_when: You are setting opex and hiring plans for a smaller store (roughly $50k-$300k/month) and must protect working capital for inventory.

cards.title: Treat first-purchase liquidity as the ecommerce norm, not the service-business norm
cards.summary: Unlike services where payback can stretch over months, consumer ecommerce brands should aim to be as profitable and liquid as possible on the first purchase because consumer stickiness is weak.
cards.use_when: You are setting payback expectations and acquisition targets, and deciding whether to accept a long first-purchase payback period.

cards.title: Use owned channels for returning revenue while accepting that new acquisition is rented
cards.summary: Email, SMS, community and brand reduce dependence on paid traffic for repeat revenue, but the source argues new-customer acquisition almost always involves renting attention.
cards.use_when: You are allocating effort between paid acquisition and list/community ownership, or pushback arises that paid should be abandoned in favour of owned channels.

cards.title: Timestamp and measure big structural changes against CAC and LTGP
cards.summary: Every major business change — new agency, new channel, new product launch, heavier ad volume — should be dated and then read back against the CAC and LTGP historical series to see if the ratio improved.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to repeat, roll back or expand an investment such as a product launch, a new ad platform, or a change in creative partner.

cards.title: Smoke test angle validation with static image ads
cards.summary: Use one product-on-white image with different text call-outs to cheaply identify which value prop or angle earns clicks before investing in video.
cards.use_when: New product launch or angle selection: you have a modest test budget and need to find which value proposition makes people click before spending on video production.

cards.title: Diagnose price before scaling spend
cards.summary: Read cheap front-end click and cart metrics first; if traffic is cost-effective and carts still abandon, the price or offer is the problem, not the ad.
cards.use_when: Early-stage acquisition: deciding whether to spend more budget or change pricing after a first test tranche.

cards.title: Tranches of cash: define what each test budget must uncover
cards.summary: Frame your ad spend as learning tranches — a $10k tranche and a $500 tranche both buy the same lessons, just at different speeds.
cards.use_when: Budget planning for a launch or a channel test: deciding how much to allocate and what questions the money must answer before it's gone.

cards.title: CAC targets anchored to LTV, not a universal number
cards.summary: Set target CAC from known customer lifespan and repeat behaviour, and accept a loss on first acquisition only when the backend justifies it.
cards.use_when: Acquisition planning: deciding your target and ceiling CAC, and whether to run first-purchase-profitable or loss-leading campaigns.

cards.title: Organise the ad account by story, not by funnel stage
cards.summary: Replace strict top/middle/bottom funnel segmentation with asset-and-angle folders that carry one consistent story from ad to landing page.
cards.use_when: Account structure decisions for paid social: how to name, group and route campaigns and how much to rely on audience segmentation.

cards.title: Creative as the new targeting
cards.summary: Build ads whose cast, setting and language mirror the region and identity of the audience you're buying, because narrative now does the targeting work.
cards.use_when: Creative direction and casting for paid social: choosing who appears in ads and which regional variants to produce.

cards.title: Design creative natively for each placement
cards.summary: Build and brief separate assets for 4x5 and 9x16 placements instead of letting a square ad with cut-off captions run everywhere.
cards.use_when: Ad production and briefing: fixing poor performance caused by mismatched aspect ratios and unreadable captions on Reels and Stories.

cards.title: Make the media buyer a P&L-aware creative strategist
cards.summary: Collapse the pod into a media buyer who also owns creative strategy and sees the P&L, with designers and editors supporting them.
cards.use_when: Team design for paid acquisition: deciding the roles needed to run ads and what performance reporting the buyer should own.

cards.title: Run a weekly creative volume target tied to spend
cards.summary: Measure new assets launched and winners that attract spend, then staff against the volume the season and profitability require.
cards.use_when: Creative operations and resourcing: setting a weekly production target and deciding when to hire editors or creators.

cards.title: Think about the funnel in numbers: 70/30 to 90/10
cards.summary: Split spend between proven winners and tests, moving from 70/30 toward 90/10 or 100/0 when company performance is weak.
cards.use_when: Allocating budget inside a paid social account: how much to keep on convictions and how much to reserve for new tests.

cards.title: Judge ads on multiple KPIs, not dashboard profit alone
cards.summary: Combine CAC, email/text capture and CPM to decide which ads to keep, and blend results across channels rather than killing an ad on one platform's ROAS.
cards.use_when: Ad reporting and optimisation: deciding whether to switch off an ad or channel that looks unprofitable on its own dashboard.

cards.title: Match site experience to customer history
cards.summary: Show first-time, returning and high-value visitors different SKUs and messages based on what they have already bought.
cards.use_when: Site merchandising and CRM: deciding what a visitor sees on arrival based on purchase history.

cards.title: Fix the homepage for your SKU count
cards.summary: Low-SKU stores should make the landing page almost a one-product conversion page; high-SKU stores should lead with offer, then bundles, then categories.
cards.use_when: Homepage and landing page design: structuring the first screens of a store based on how many products you sell.

cards.title: Replace blank white PDP first images with lifestyle imagery
cards.summary: A product page whose hero is a plain product on white wastes prime real estate that could carry lifestyle context and a strong headline.
cards.use_when: PDP optimisation: revising the first image and adjacent copy on a product page.

cards.title: Use clipping marketplaces to scale distribution cheaply
cards.summary: Buy fixed-budget clip campaigns from low-cost creators who post to their own pages, paying only for approved posts and capped at your budget even if clips go viral.
cards.use_when: Acquisition creative sourcing: testing a paid clipper model to add volume and impressions beyond your own accounts.

cards.title: Set up a testing pipeline and organic posting habit
cards.summary: Run a repeating image-to-video test tree across value props, male/female presenters and regions, and keep posting organically because it supports the ad account.
cards.use_when: Standing up a paid social testing process and deciding whether organic posting is worth the time for an ecommerce brand.

cards.title: Build an always-on creative bench and 30-day asset runway
cards.summary: Keep testing and producing even when you have winners, because the account is the lifeline of new customers and stopping is not an option.
cards.use_when: Creative and media planning over a month or quarter: keeping a rotating pipeline rather than scheduling one-off production bursts.

cards.title: Brief editors and designers with references plus brand context
cards.summary: Untrained editors replicate a reference pixel-by-pixel; the editor you want understands the reference, your brand and how to improve on it.
cards.use_when: Creative production and outsourcing: writing briefs for external creative help who understand performance marketing.

cards.title: Learn the ad account yourself before hiring out
cards.summary: Founders and leadership should run ads up to roughly $10k-$30k of spend so they can ask better questions and avoid paying management on top of test budget.
cards.use_when: Early paid acquisition: deciding whether to manage ads internally or hand them to an agency or freelancer.

cards.title: Track daily burn, discount rate and high-value orders together
cards.summary: Understand your daily burn and your discount percent of sales so rising revenue doesn't hide shrinking margin.
cards.use_when: Finance and acquisition coordination: setting daily tracking and deciding when to pull ad spend or run promos.

cards.title: PDP hero image: lifestyle over white-background product shot
cards.summary: Treat the first PDP image as a split-testable asset and favor lifestyle/in-use imagery over sterile white-background shots.
cards.use_when: Designing or A/B testing the lead image and above-the-fold layout on a product detail page.

cards.title: Increase AOV on the PDP with frequently-bought-together blocks
cards.summary: Use bundled and multi-pack blocks on product pages to raise average order value, especially for multi-SKU catalogs.
cards.use_when: Merchandising a PDP or cart for a brand with multiple SKUs, packs, or add-on options.

cards.title: Strategic homepage offer placement by margin and inventory
cards.summary: Choose which offer occupies the homepage hero based on margin and the inventory you most need to move, not just what is newest.
cards.use_when: Deciding which product, bundle, or offer to feature in the homepage hero or primary merchandising slot.

cards.title: Designing acquisition offers for a high-CPM environment
cards.summary: With CPMs running $35–$45 in the source's dataset, structure offers that give new customers something they cannot get elsewhere and set up later purchases.
cards.use_when: Building a new-customer acquisition offer when paid media costs are high and first-order economics are tight.
